{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Licensed Technology / FX Platform Agreement

**To:** Deal team (Customer side)  
**From:** In-house counsel  
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings only

---

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and verified 19 findings. Six rules are met; ten clauses deviate on material terms and two expected protections are missing entirely.

The risk profile is heavily one-sided. Three critical items drive it: there is no Licensor indemnity anywhere in the Agreement (Article XII runs one way from us, and Article XIII expressly disclaims Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement); the liability cap protects Licensor only and sits at one half of amounts paid while our exposure is uncapped and expanded by the broad indemnity; and ownership is one-way, with the custom development we fund under Article VII(b) captured as Licensor-owned "Derivative Work" and no confirmation that we retain our data or pre-existing IP.

The term and exit architecture compounds this: a 36-month Initial Period with no Licensee convenience right, a unilateral Licensor option to extend by a further seven years, automatic termination of the Agreement and all licences on our Change of Control, a blanket bar on our assignment with no affiliate or M&A carve-out, and no post-termination transition assistance or return of our trading data (Article XXI runs only in Licensor's favour). The platform is also provided wholly "AS IS" with no conformance warranty, and usage audits are subject to no frequency limit.

On the positive side, the commercial core is clean: the licence is non-exclusive both ways, fees are purely usage-based with no minimum commitment, take-or-pay or liquidated damages, no MFN or non-compete binds us, and governing law and venue are New York with exclusive New York state and federal courts.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability (cap, mutuality, carve-outs) | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | GENERAL PROVISIONS |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § I CERTAIN DEFINITIONS |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | WARRANTY DISCLAIMER |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | 50+ US$5.00 |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | GENERAL PROVISIONS |
| Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | 50+ US$5.00 |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | GENERAL PROVISIONS |

### Notes on the material deviations

- **INDEMN (critical).** Article XII is a wholly one-way indemnity from us to Licensor covering any exercise of the licence rights, the conduct of our business and any breach by us; there is no Licensor indemnity anywhere, and Article XIII states Licensor shall in no circumstance be liable for claims that use of the Licensed Technology infringes third-party IP. We add the standard Licensor defence/indemnity (third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) expressly outside the Article XIII cap, and narrow our own indemnity to breach of the licence restrictions, our breach of law and content we supply.
- **IP (critical).** Licensor retaining its platform IP is expected, but "Derivative Work" sweeps in additions, modifications and enhancements based on the Licensed Technology — including the client front end and enhancements we fund under Article VII(b) — leaving us with only a non-exclusive, Field-of-Use-limited licence for the term. We add a carve-out: we retain our data and pre-existing IP with no assignment or joint ownership, and customizations we fund are assigned to us with Licensor retaining pre-existing platform IP and granting a perpetual royalty-free licence to embedded Licensor IP.
- **LOL-CAP (critical).** The cap protects Licensor only, at one half of amounts paid, with a one-way consequential-damages exclusion and no carve-outs. We make the cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, mutualize the consequential-damages exclusion, and add the standard uncapped Excluded Claims, with our fee obligations excluded from the cap.
- **ASSIGN (high).** Section (c) bars our assignment outright with no affiliate or M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard, while leaving Licensor free to assign; Article XX makes our Change of Control an automatic termination event. We add the Affiliate/successor carve-out on notice, make consent mutual and not unreasonably withheld (barring assignment to our competitors), and delete the change-of-control termination trigger.
- **LICENSE (high).** The grant reaches the Licensee's employees only, excluding our Affiliates and the contractors and introducing brokers who operate the Platform for us, and Article IV permits immediate termination for any breach with no cure period. We extend the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, confirm successor transfer in an M&A transaction, and limit revocation to uncured material breach; Affiliate coverage on written notice is our fallback.
- **T4C (high).** We are committed for 36 months (extendable a further seven years at Licensor's option) with no convenience exit. We add a 30-day Licensee convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
- **WARRANTY (medium).** The platform is provided "AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed, including error-free operation and correction of nonconformities; only a "commercially reasonable efforts" Error Correction covenant remains, with no remedy. We carve express warranties out of the disclaimer and add a documentation-conformance warranty with repair, replace or refund, plus workmanlike performance, legal compliance and no-malicious-code; 90 days software / 30 days services is available as a fallback.
- **RENEWAL (medium).** Licensor holds a unilateral option to extend by seven years, with no cap on renewal pricing; subsections II and III of the same Article contemplate extension only by mutual agreement, so the option sentence is internally inconsistent. We conform it to mutual 12-month renewals with a CPI/3% uplift cap.
- **NOSOLICIT (medium).** The restriction is one-way, runs for the Term plus three years and covers every Licensor and Affiliate employee, and is backed by the Article XI injunctive-relief clause. The general-advertisement and unsolicited-inquiry carve-outs are helpful but do not cure duration or scope. We propose a mutual 12-month restriction limited to personnel directly involved.
- **AUDIT (medium).** The Article V(IV)(b) mechanic is otherwise good — independent CPA selected by mutual agreement, records only, cost on Licensor absent a 5% discrepancy — but there is no frequency limit at all. We cap audits at once per 12 months, during business hours, subject to confidentiality.
- **TRANSITION (missing).** Article XXI requires us to return all Licensed Technology and Confidential Information within five days with officer certification, with no reciprocal migration assistance or return of our trading data. We insert a new Article XXI(c): up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, return of Licensee Data in machine-readable format within 30 days, then certified deletion; 90 days' assistance is our fallback.
- **INSURANCE (missing).** The only reference to insurance is a pass-through of charges payable by us. We insert a short insurance covenant as a new General Provisions subsection, with E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M offered as the fallback.

---

## Walk-away items

The following findings sit in, or approach, walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **No Vendor IP indemnity plus a one-way Customer indemnity** (INDEMN) — compounded by the Article XIII exclusion of Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement.
2. **Customer uncapped / Vendor cap below six months' fees** (LOL-CAP).
3. **Vendor right to terminate on Customer change of control, and blanket bar on Customer assignment** (ASSIGN).
4. **No Customer termination for convenience in a multi-year term** (T4C).
5. **Unilateral multi-year (seven-year) renewal option we cannot opt out of** (RENEWAL) — worse than the auto-renewal walk-away trigger.
6. **"AS IS" delivery with no conformance warranty or remedy** (WARRANTY).
7. **Unlimited audit frequency** (AUDIT).
8. **Non-solicit exceeding 24 months and covering all Vendor personnel** (NOSOLICIT).
9. **No data return or transition assistance on exit** (TRANSITION) — material given our market data and trade tickets flow through the hosted platform.
10. **No vendor insurance of any kind** (INSURANCE).

IP ownership of the customizations we fund (IP) and the exclusion of our Affiliates and contractors from the licence grant (LICENSE) fail both the preferred and fallback positions and should be resolved alongside the above.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the ten deviations and two missing clauses, in the priority order above, with playbook fallbacks flagged in comments where offered (Affiliate coverage on notice; 90-day transition assistance; 90-day/30-day warranty; E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M).
2. **Lead negotiation on the three critical items** — Licensor indemnity, mutual capped liability, and ownership of funded customizations and our data. These are interdependent: the indemnity has no content unless it sits outside the Article XIII cap.
3. **Package the exit issues** (T4C, RENEWAL, ASSIGN change of control, TRANSITION) as a single "term and exit" ask, since the 36-month lock, seven-year Licensor option, change-of-control termination and absence of data return operate together.
4. **Confirm internally** the commercial appetite for the Article VII(b) custom development spend and the Article VII/XXII arrangements if Licensor resists assignment of funded customizations.
5. **Refer the Article XXII right of first refusal** over a sale of, or merger involving, our business to corporate/M&A colleagues — the reviewing team confirmed it is outside the exclusivity and non-compete rules and was not assessed under the assignment rule.
6. **No action required** on exclusivity, liquidated damages, non-compete, governing law, MFN or minimum commitments; we should resist any counterparty attempt to reopen these, as each currently sits at our preferred position."}
